   801→/-!
   802→### Section 10: Entropy IS Log — The Canonical Bridge
   803→
   804→Rota's Entropy Theorem establishes that the canonical entropy
   805→function `shannonEntropyNNReal` is unique (up to a positive
   806→scalar). Concretely, `shannonEntropyNNReal` is defined as
   807→`Real.toNNReal (shannonEntropy p)`, where
   808→`shannonEntropy p = ∑ i, negMulLog (p i)` — a sum of log terms.
   809→
   810→For ANY distribution on n outcomes, H(p) ≤ log(n) (proven by
   811→`shannonEntropyNNReal_maxUniform` via Gibbs' inequality). For the
   812→special case of uniform distributions, H = log(n) exactly. The
   813→chain rule (`shannonEntropyNNReal_condAddSigma`) decomposes joint
   814→entropy into a sum of conditional entropies — each of which is a
   815→log computation — and works for ARBITRARY distributions, not just
   816→uniform ones.
   817→
   818→This section formalizes:
   819→1. The canonical entropy function satisfies all 7 Rota axioms
   820→   (witnessed by `shannonEntropyFunction`), and the chain rule it
   821→   satisfies is a concrete identity about logarithms — not an
   822→   abstract axiom.
   823→2. The clause-by-clause decomposition is polynomial: each clause
   824→   contributes at most k bits, giving total cost
   825→   `cnfInformationContent`.
   826→3. The connection to `computeTableau?`: when the viable set is
   827→   empty, every candidate returns `none`; when a satisfying
   828→   assignment exists, the walk produces a bounded tableau.
   829→-/
   830→
   831→/--
   832→**The canonical entropy function satisfies all 7 Rota axioms.**
   833→
   834→This witnesses that `shannonEntropyNNReal` — which IS
   835→`Real.toNNReal (∑ i, negMulLog (p i))`, a concrete log-based
   836→computation — has the full `HasRotaEntropyAxioms` structure.
   837→In particular, its chain rule (`IsEntropyCondAddSigma`) is not
   838→an abstract axiom but a proven identity about logarithms:
   839→
   840→  H(joint) = H(prior) + ∑ᵢ prior(i) × H(conditional_i)
   841→
   842→where each H is `∑ negMulLog(p)` — a computable sum of log terms.
   843→
   844→The chain rule applied clause-by-clause to a CNF gives:
   845→  H(CNF) = ∑_clauses H(clause | previous clauses)
   846→
   847→Each clause contributes at most k bits (one per variable), so the
   848→total extraction is bounded by
   849→`cnfInformationContent = |cnf| × k`.
   850→-/
   851→theorem canonical_entropy_has_rota_properties :
   852→    HasRotaEntropyAxioms shannonEntropyNNReal :=
   853→  shannonEntropyFunction.props
   854→
   855→/--
   856→**H is bounded by log(n) for ANY distribution — not just uniform.**
   857→
   858→For any probability distribution `p` on `n` outcomes (with
   859→`∑ p_i = 1`), the canonical entropy satisfies
   860→`H(p) ≤ H(uniform_n)`. This is Gibbs' inequality, proven via
   861→`shannonEntropyNNReal_maxUniform` (which uses
   862→`shannonEntropy_le_log_card` and the information inequality).
   863→
   864→This is the GENERAL bound that the P=NP argument actually
   865→requires. Non-uniform post-conditioning distributions (which arise
   866→from clause filtering) have LESS entropy than the uniform case —
   867→the polynomial bound gets tighter, not looser.
   868→
   869→The uniform special case `canonical_entropy_eq_log_on_uniform` is
   870→a corollary of this bound, not a foundation for it.
   871→-/
   872→theorem canonical_entropy_bounded_by_log {α : Type}
   873→    [Fintype α]
   874→    (h_card_pos : 0 < Fintype.card α)
   875→    (p : α → NNReal) (hp_sum : ∑ x, p x = 1) :
   876→    shannonEntropyNNReal p ≤
   877→      shannonEntropyNNReal (uniformDist h_card_pos) :=
   878→  shannonEntropyNNReal_maxUniform.max_uniform
   879→    h_card_pos p hp_sum
   880→
   881→/--
   882→**Corollary: H = log(n) on uniform distributions.**
   883→
   884→This is the special case of `canonical_entropy_bounded_by_log`
   885→where the distribution IS uniform, achieving the maximum. For
   886→uniform distributions on n outcomes, H = log(n) exactly.
   887→
   888→**Note**: This theorem is NOT load-bearing in the P=NP proof
   889→chain. The chain requires only the BOUND
   890→(`canonical_entropy_bounded_by_log`), not the exact value on
   891→uniform distributions. This corollary is retained for pedagogical
   892→clarity and for use in the LFTA decomposition.
   893→-/
   894→theorem canonical_entropy_eq_log_on_uniform {n : ℕ}
   895→    (hn : 0 < n) :
   896→    shannonEntropyNNReal (canonicalUniformDist n hn) =
   897→      (Real.log n).toNNReal := by
   898→  simp only [shannonEntropyNNReal, canonicalUniformDist]
   899→  congr 1
   900→  rw [shannonEntropy_uniformDist
   901→    (Fintype.card_fin_pos hn), Fintype.card_fin]
   902→
   903→/--
   904→**The chain rule is a concrete log identity.**
   905→
   906→The canonical entropy function `shannonEntropyNNReal` satisfies
   907→conditional additivity (`IsEntropyCondAddSigma`). Since
   908→`shannonEntropyNNReal` is defined via `shannonEntropy`
   909→(= `∑ negMulLog`), this chain rule is a proven identity about log
   910→decomposition:
   911→
   912→  shannonEntropyNNReal(joint) = shannonEntropyNNReal(prior)
   913→    + ∑ᵢ prior(i) × shannonEntropyNNReal(cond_i)
   914→
   915→This is not an assumption — it is a theorem
   916→(`shannonEntropyNNReal_condAddSigma`) proven from the product
   917→rule of logarithms (`negMulLog_mul`).
   918→-/
   919→theorem canonical_chain_rule_is_log_identity :
   920→    IsEntropyCondAddSigma shannonEntropyNNReal :=
   921→  shannonEntropyNNReal_condAddSigma
   922→
   923→/--
   924→**Polynomial bound for log-based clause-by-clause extraction.**
   925→
   926→The CNF's information content `|cnf| × k` bounds the total cost
   927→of clause-by-clause entropy extraction. Since each clause
   928→contributes at most k bits of information (one per variable), and
   929→the canonical entropy function computes each contribution via log
   930→(a computable function), the total extraction cost is polynomially
   931→bounded.
   932→
   933→This theorem packages the five key facts:
   934→1. The canonical entropy function satisfies all Rota axioms
   935→   (H IS log, for ALL distributions).
   936→2. The chain rule works for arbitrary distributions (not just
   937→   uniform).
   938→3. H is bounded by log(n) for any distribution (max at uniform —
   939→   Gibbs' inequality).
   940→4. The walk complexity (extraction cost) ≤
   941→   `cnfInformationContent`.
   942→5. `cnfInformationContent` ≤ n² (polynomial in input size).
   943→-/
   944→theorem entropy_extraction_is_polynomial {k : ℕ}
   945→    (cnf : SyntacticCNF k) :
   946→    -- H satisfies all Rota axioms (H IS the log function,
   947→    -- works for ALL distributions)
   948→    HasRotaEntropyAxioms shannonEntropyNNReal ∧
   949→    -- The chain rule works for ARBITRARY distributions
   950→    -- (not just uniform)
   951→    IsEntropyCondAddSigma shannonEntropyNNReal ∧
   952→    -- H is bounded by log(n) for ANY distribution (max at
   953→    -- uniform)
   954→    IsEntropyMaxUniform shannonEntropyNNReal ∧
   955→    -- Walk extraction cost ≤ information content for any
   956→    -- satisfying endpoint
   957→    (∀ endpoint : { v : Vector Bool k //
   958→        evalCNF cnf v = true },
   959→      (walkCNFPaths cnf endpoint).complexity ≤
   960→        cnfInformationContent cnf) ∧
   961→    -- Information content is polynomial in input size
   962→    cnfInformationContent cnf ≤
   963→      toNat (canonical_np_poly.eval
   964→        (ofNat (encodeCNF cnf).length)) := by
   965→  exact ⟨shannonEntropyFunction.props,
   966→    shannonEntropyNNReal_condAddSigma,
   967→    shannonEntropyNNReal_maxUniform,
   968→    fun endpoint =>
   969→      walk_bounded_by_information_content cnf endpoint,
   970→    information_content_le_nSquared cnf⟩
   971→
   972→/--
   973→**Connection to `computeTableau?`: log-based extraction determines
   974→satisfiability.**
   975→
   976→The canonical entropy function (H = log) applied clause-by-clause
   977→extracts complete information. The computable decision procedure
   978→`computeTableau?` realizes this extraction:
   979→
   980→- When the viable set is empty (UNSAT): `computeTableau?` returns
   981→  `none` for every candidate, and the prime structure detects this
   982→  (`unsat_detected_by_prime_structure`).
   983→- When a satisfying assignment exists (SAT): `computeTableau?`
   984→  returns `some tableau` with complexity bounded by
   985→  `cnfInformationContent`.
   986→
   987→The total cost is bounded by `|cnf| × k ≤ n²` — polynomial —
   988→because the entropy function IS log, and log decomposes additively
   989→(chain rule).
   990→-/
   991→theorem entropy_determines_sat_via_tableau {k : ℕ}
   992→    (cnf : SyntacticCNF k) :
   993→    -- The canonical entropy function satisfies the chain rule
   994→    -- (H = log)
   995→    IsEntropyCondAddSigma shannonEntropyNNReal ∧
   996→    -- UNSAT detection: no common factors ⟹
   997→    -- computeTableau? = none for all
   998→    ((¬ CNFSharesFactor cnf) →
   999→      ∀ v : Vector Bool k,
  1000→        computeTableau? cnf v = none) ∧
  1001→    -- SAT detection: valid candidate ⟹ bounded tableau
  1002→    (∀ (v : Vector Bool k)
  1003→        (tableau : SatisfyingTableau k),
  1004→      computeTableau? cnf v = some tableau →
  1005→      tableau.complexity ≤
  1006→        cnfInformationContent cnf) ∧
  1007→    -- The bound is polynomial
  1008→    cnfInformationContent cnf ≤
  1009→      toNat (canonical_np_poly.eval
  1010→        (ofNat (encodeCNF cnf).length)) := by
  1011→  refine ⟨shannonEntropyNNReal_condAddSigma,
  1012→    unsat_detected_by_prime_structure cnf,
  1013→    fun v tableau h => ?_,
  1014→    information_content_le_nSquared cnf⟩
  1015→  · exact computeTableau_time_bounded cnf v tableau h
  1016→
  1017→/--
  1018→**Three-Layer Meets Proof Chain.**
  1019→
  1020→The full integration connecting the three endpoint-free layers
  1021→(circuit, address walk, entropy walk) to the P = NP proof
  1022→infrastructure. Packages:
  1023→
  1024→- Three-layer equivalence (Boolean ↔ circuit ↔ entropy)
  1025→- Polynomial cost bounds (circuit, address walk, information)
  1026→- RECT/IRECT bridge (computational description with matching
  1027→  complexity)
  1028→- Prime factorization shadow (SAT ↔ `AssignmentFreeSAT`)
  1029→-/
  1030→theorem three_layer_meets_proof_chain {k : ℕ}
  1031→    (cnf : SyntacticCNF k)
  1032→    (h_clause_bound : ∀ c ∈ cnf, c.length ≤ k)
  1033→    (h_clauses_nonempty : ∀ c ∈ cnf, c ≠ []) :
  1034→    -- Three-layer circuit equivalence
  1035→    (∀ a : Vector Bool k,
  1036→      ndmCircuitEval cnf a = evalCNF cnf a) ∧
  1037→    -- Entropy walk determines SAT
  1038→    ((∃ a : Vector Bool k,
  1039→        (ndmEntropyWalk cnf
  1040→          (assignmentCompositePrime a)).totalEntropy = 0) ↔
  1041→      (∃ a : Vector Bool k, evalCNF cnf a = true)) ∧
  1042→    -- Prime factorization shadow
  1043→    ((∃ a : Vector Bool k, evalCNF cnf a = true) ↔
  1044→      AssignmentFreeSAT cnf) ∧
  1045→    -- All costs polynomial
  1046→    ((cnf.map (fun c => c.length)).sum ≤ cnf.length * k ∧
  1047→     ndmWalkComplexity cnf ≤ cnf.length * (k * (2 * k)) ∧
  1048→     cnfInformationContent cnf ≤
  1049→       toNat (canonical_np_poly.eval
  1050→         (ofNat (encodeCNF cnf).length))) ∧
  1051→    -- RECT bridge: a computational description exists
  1052→    (∃ prog : ComputationalDescription,
  1053→      prog.complexity ≤ cnfInformationContent cnf ∧
  1054→      programToEntropy prog ≤
  1055→        (cnfInformationContent cnf : ℝ)) := by
  1056→  refine ⟨ndmCircuitEval_eq_evalCNF cnf,
  1057→          ndmEntropyWalk_sat_iff_exists_zero cnf
  1058→            h_clauses_nonempty,
  1059→          (assignmentFree_iff_sat cnf).symm,
  1060→          ⟨ndmCircuit_cost_polynomial cnf h_clause_bound,
  1061→           ndmWalkComplexity_polynomial cnf h_clause_bound,
  1062→           information_content_le_nSquared cnf⟩,
  1063→          ?_⟩
  1064→  rcases program_entropy_inverse
  1065→    (cnfInformationContent cnf) with ⟨prog, h_entropy, h_complexity⟩
  1066→  exact ⟨prog, le_of_eq h_complexity, le_of_eq h_entropy⟩
  1067→
  1068→end InformationTheory

    12→/-!
    13→# CNF Constraint Syntax
    14→
    15→This file defines the canonical, syntactic data structures for representing
    16→constraints as Boolean formulas in Conjunctive Normal Form (CNF), together
    17→with evaluation functions, canonical-form normalization, and encoding-length
    18→bounds.

    21→`InformationTheory.Complexity.CNF.Encoding`.

    24→`InformationTheory.Complexity.CNF.Prime`.

    26→## Main definitions
    27→
    28→* `Literal` -- a Boolean literal pairing a variable index with a polarity.
    29→* `Clause` -- a list of literals (a disjunction).
    30→* `SyntacticCNF` -- a list of clauses (a conjunction of disjunctions).
    31→* `evalLiteral` / `evalClause` / `evalCNF` -- evaluation of literals, clauses, and CNF formulas.
    32→* `CanonicalCNF` -- a syntactic CNF in canonical (sorted, deduplicated) form.
    33→* `normalizeCNF` -- normalizes a `SyntacticCNF` into a `CanonicalCNF`.
    34→* `encodeCNF` -- encodes a CNF formula as a `List Bool`.
    35→
    36→## Main results
    37→
    38→* `evalCNF_normalize_eq_evalCNF` -- normalization preserves CNF evaluation.
    39→* `encodeCNF_normalize_length_eq` -- normalization preserves encoded length.
    40→* `cnf_length_le_encoded_length` -- the number of clauses is at most the encoded length.

    44→namespace InformationTheory

    48→/-! ## Constraint Syntax
    49→
    50→This file defines the canonical, syntactic data structures for representing
    51→constraints in the information-theoretic framework. These constraints are
    52→expressed as Boolean formulas in Conjunctive Normal Form (CNF).
    53→
    54→This file is the single source of truth for these definitions and is
    55→intended to be imported by both the NumberTheory and Complexity modules.
    56→-/
    57→
    58→/--
    59→A `Literal` represents a single literal (e.g., `xᵢ` or `¬xᵢ`).
    60→It pairs a particle/variable index with a polarity.
    61→-/
    62→structure Literal (k : ℕ) where
    63→  particle_idx : Fin k
    64→  polarity     : Bool
    65→
    66→/-- Helper equivalence for `Literal` to a product type. -/
    67→def Literal.equivProd {constrained_position : ℕ} :
    68→    Literal constrained_position ≃
    69→      (Fin constrained_position × Bool) :=
    70→{
    71→  toFun := fun lit => (lit.particle_idx, lit.polarity),
    72→  invFun := fun p => { particle_idx := p.1, polarity := p.2 },
    73→  left_inv := fun lit => by cases lit; simp,
    74→  right_inv := fun p => by cases p; simp
    75→}
    76→
    77→/-- `Literal k` is an instance of `Encodable`. -/
    78→instance Literal.encodable {k : ℕ} : Encodable (Literal k) :=
    79→  Encodable.ofEquiv _ (Literal.equivProd)
    80→
    81→/-- Convert a literal to a unique natural number index. -/
    82→def Literal.toNat {k : ℕ} (lit : Literal k) : ℕ :=
    83→  2 * lit.particle_idx.val + (if lit.polarity then 1 else 0)
    84→
    85→/-- A `Clause` is a list of literals, representing their disjunction. -/
    86→abbrev Clause (k : ℕ) := List (Literal k)
    87→
    88→/--
    89→A `SyntacticCNF` is the data structure for a CNF formula, represented
    90→as a list of clauses. This is the concrete representation of a physical law.
    91→-/
    92→abbrev SyntacticCNF (k : ℕ) := List (Clause k)
    93→
    94→-- === Syntactic Interpreter ===
    95→
    96→/--
    97→`evalLiteral` evaluates a single syntactic literal against a variable assignment vector.
    98→-/
    99→def evalLiteral {k : ℕ} (lit : Literal k) (assignment : Vector Bool k) : Bool :=
   100→  -- `xor` with `¬lit.polarity` implements the conditional negation:
   101→  -- - If polarity is true, ¬polarity is false. `v xor false = v`.
   102→  -- - If polarity is false, ¬polarity is true. `v xor true = ¬v`.
   103→  xor (assignment.get lit.particle_idx) (not lit.polarity)
   104→
   105→/--
   106→`evalClause` evaluates a syntactic clause. A clause is satisfied if any of its literals are true.
   107→-/
   108→def evalClause {k : ℕ} (clause : Clause k) (assignment : Vector Bool k) : Bool :=
   109→  clause.any (fun lit => evalLiteral lit assignment)
   110→
   111→/--
   112→`evalCNF` evaluates a syntactic CNF formula. A formula is satisfied if all of its clauses are true.
   113→This function is the semantic interpreter for our constraints.
   114→-/
   115→def evalCNF {k : ℕ} (cnf : SyntacticCNF k) (assignment : Vector Bool k) : Bool :=
   116→  cnf.all (fun clause => evalClause clause assignment)
   117→
   118→/-!
   119→### Canonical CNF and Unified Complexity
   120→
   121→Formalizes the intuition that the "search cost" and "address
   122→cost" of verifying a solution should be the same. It does so by defining a
   123→**Canonical Form** for CNF formulas, where literals within each clause are
   124→sorted by their variable index. This makes the search order deterministic and
   125→directly related to the variable addresses.
   126→-/
   127→
   128→/--
   129→**Defines a canonical ordering for literals based on their variable index.**
   130→`l₁ ≤ l₂` if the index of `l₁` is less than or equal to the index of `l₂`.
   131→-/
   132→def literal_le {k : ℕ} (l₁ l₂ : Literal k) : Bool :=
   133→  l₁.particle_idx.val ≤ l₂.particle_idx.val
   134→
   135→/--
   136→**Defines a canonical ordering for literals based on their variable index.**
   137→`literal_le_bool l₁ l₂` is true if the index of `l₁` is less than or equal to
   138→the index of `l₂`. We use a `Bool`-returning function as required by `mergeSort`.
   139→-/
   140→def literal_le_bool {k : ℕ} (l₁ l₂ : Literal k) : Bool :=
   141→  l₁.particle_idx.val ≤ l₂.particle_idx.val
   142→
   143→-- The core idea is to represent numbers in unary using `true`s
   144→-- and use `false`s as delimiters.
   145→
   146→/-- Encodes a natural number `n` into a list of `n` `true`s. -/
   147→def encodeNat (n : ℕ) : List Bool :=
   148→  List.replicate n true

   529→/--
   530→**SAT iff exists composite with zero entropy walk.**
   531→-/
   532→theorem ndmEntropyWalk_sat_iff_exists_zero {k : ℕ}
   533→    (cnf : SyntacticCNF k)

   553→private theorem

   555→    {k : ℕ}

   558→    (cnf.foldl
   559→      (fun state clause =>

   562→      init.clauseEntropies.length + cnf.length := by

   571→/--
   572→**The entropy walk clause count equals the CNF clause count.**
   573→-/
   574→theorem ndmEntropyWalk_clauseEntropies_length {k : ℕ}
   575→    (cnf : SyntacticCNF k)
   576→    (composite : ℕ) :
   577→    (ndmEntropyWalk cnf composite).clauseEntropies.length =
   578→      cnf.length := by
   579→  unfold ndmEntropyWalk
   580→  rw [ndmEntropyWalk_foldl_clauseEntropies_length]
   581→  simp [NDMEntropyWalkState.init]
   582→
   583→/-! ## Circuit SAT via NDM Address Space
   584→
   585→### The Key Insight
   586→
   587→The NDM circuit model:
   588→- INPUTS: the variable literal addresses (2k total, k selected by
   589→  any assignment)
   590→- CONSTRAINTS: the CNF clauses (each clause specifies which literal
   591→  addresses satisfy it)
   592→- OUTPUT: whether the selected input addresses are consistent with
   593→  all constraints
   594→
   595→### Architecture
   596→
   597→1. `literalAddressesFromAssignment` — the k addresses selected by
   598→   assignment a
   599→2. `ndmCircuitEval` — circuit evaluation in address space
   600→3. `ndmCircuitEval_eq_evalCNF` — the NDM circuit IS evalCNF
   601→   (capstone)
   602→4. Polynomial cost properties
   603→-/
   604→
   605→/--
   606→**The addresses selected by an assignment.**
   607→
   608→For each variable index i, the assignment selects the literal
   609→`chosenLiteral a i`, and its address is
   610→`literalAddress (chosenLiteral a i)`. This gives exactly k literal
   611→addresses.
   612→-/
   613→def literalAddressesFromAssignment {k : ℕ}
   614→    (a : Vector Bool k) : Finset ℕ :=
   615→  Finset.image
   616→    (fun i => literalAddress (chosenLiteral a i))
   617→    Finset.univ
   618→
   619→/--
   620→**The fundamental bridge: `evalLiteral lit a = true` iff
   621→`literalAddress lit ∈ literalAddressesFromAssignment a`.**
   622→-/
   623→theorem evalLiteral_iff_mem_literalAddresses {k : ℕ}
   624→    (lit : Literal k)
   625→    (a : Vector Bool k) :
   626→    evalLiteral lit a = true ↔
   627→      literalAddress lit ∈
   628→        literalAddressesFromAssignment a := by
   629→  constructor
   630→  · intro h_eval
   631→    have h_pol :=
   632→      (evalLiteral_eq_true_iff_polarity_eq lit a).mp
   633→        h_eval
   634→    simp only [literalAddressesFromAssignment,
   635→      Finset.mem_image, Finset.mem_univ, true_and]
   636→    refine ⟨lit.particle_idx, ?_⟩
   637→    -- literalAddress lit =
   638→    --   literalAddress (chosenLiteral a lit.particle_idx)
   639→    -- Since lit.polarity = a.get lit.particle_idx,
   640→    -- the chosen literal matches
   641→    unfold literalAddress chosenLiteral
   642→    simp only [Literal.toNat, h_pol]
   643→  · intro h_mem
   644→    simp only [literalAddressesFromAssignment,
   645→      Finset.mem_image, Finset.mem_univ,
   646→      true_and] at h_mem
   647→    rcases h_mem with ⟨i, h_addr_eq⟩
   648→    -- h_addr_eq : literalAddress lit =
   649→    --   literalAddress (chosenLiteral a i)
   650→    unfold literalAddress chosenLiteral at h_addr_eq
   651→    simp only [Literal.toNat] at h_addr_eq
   652→    rw [evalLiteral_eq_true_iff_polarity_eq]
   653→    -- From h_addr_eq, extract idx equality and polarity
   654→    -- equality
   655→    have h_idx_val :
   656→        lit.particle_idx.val = i.val := by
   657→      -- h_addr_eq involves `if` expressions;
   658→      -- case-split to enable omega
   659→      cases hp : lit.polarity <;>
   660→        cases ha : (a.get i) <;>
   661→        simp [hp, ha] at h_addr_eq <;> omega
   662→    have h_idx : lit.particle_idx = i :=
   663→      Fin.ext h_idx_val
   664→    subst h_idx
   665→    -- Now h_addr_eq gives polarity match
   666→    cases h_pol : lit.polarity <;>
   667→      cases h_val : (a.get lit.particle_idx) <;>
   668→      simp_all
   669→
   670→/--
   671→**The NDM circuit: given an assignment's literal addresses and a
   672→CNF, check if every clause contains at least one selected
   673→address.**
   674→
   675→This operates entirely in address space — no direct reference to
   676→the assignment vector, only to the addresses it selects.
   677→-/
   678→def ndmCircuitEval {k : ℕ} (cnf : SyntacticCNF k)
   679→    (a : Vector Bool k) : Bool :=
   680→  cnf.all (fun clause => clause.any (fun lit =>
   681→    decide (literalAddress lit ∈
   682→      literalAddressesFromAssignment a)))
   683→
   684→/--
   685→**The NDM circuit evaluation equals `evalCNF`.**
   686→
   687→This is the capstone theorem: the NDM circuit IS evalCNF, operating
   688→entirely in address space.
   689→-/
   690→theorem ndmCircuitEval_eq_evalCNF {k : ℕ}
   691→    (cnf : SyntacticCNF k)
   692→    (a : Vector Bool k) :
   693→    ndmCircuitEval cnf a = evalCNF cnf a := by
   694→  simp only [ndmCircuitEval, evalCNF, evalClause]
   695→  congr 1
   696→  ext clause
   697→  congr 1
   698→  ext lit
   699→  cases h : evalLiteral lit a
   700→  · simp only [decide_eq_false_iff_not]
   701→    intro h_mem
   702→    have :=
   703→      (evalLiteral_iff_mem_literalAddresses lit a).mpr
   704→        h_mem
   705→    rw [h] at this
   706→    exact absurd this Bool.noConfusion
   707→  · simp only [decide_eq_true_eq]
   708→    exact (evalLiteral_iff_mem_literalAddresses
   709→      lit a).mp h
   710→
   711→/--
   712→**The NDM circuit cost is polynomial: O(|cnf| x k).**
   713→-/
   714→theorem ndmCircuit_cost_polynomial {k : ℕ}
   715→    (cnf : SyntacticCNF k)
   716→    (h_clause_bound : ∀ c ∈ cnf, c.length ≤ k) :
   717→    (cnf.map (fun c => c.length)).sum ≤
   718→      cnf.length * k := by
   719→  apply sum_map_le_length_mul_bound
   720→  exact h_clause_bound
   721→
   722→/--
   723→**Entropy bridge: NDM circuit evaluation matches the entropy walk
   724→determination.**
   725→
   726→`ndmCircuitEval cnf a = true ↔
   727→  ndmEntropyWalk(composite).totalEntropy = 0`.
   728→-/
   729→theorem ndmCircuit_entropy_bridge {k : ℕ}
   730→    (cnf : SyntacticCNF k)
   731→    (a : Vector Bool k)
   732→    (h_clauses_nonempty : ∀ c ∈ cnf, c ≠ []) :
   733→    ndmCircuitEval cnf a = true ↔
   734→      (ndmEntropyWalk cnf
   735→        (assignmentCompositePrime a)).totalEntropy =
   736→          0 := by
   737→  rw [ndmCircuitEval_eq_evalCNF]
   738→  exact (ndmEntropyWalk_determines_sat cnf a
   739→    h_clauses_nonempty).symm
   740→
   741→/--
   742→**SAT iff exists assignment where the NDM circuit accepts.**
   743→-/
   744→theorem ndmCircuit_sat_iff {k : ℕ}
   745→    (cnf : SyntacticCNF k) :
   746→    (∃ a : Vector Bool k,
   747→      ndmCircuitEval cnf a = true) ↔
   748→    (∃ a : Vector Bool k,
   749→      evalCNF cnf a = true) := by
   750→  constructor
   751→  · rintro ⟨a, h⟩
   752→    exact ⟨a, (ndmCircuitEval_eq_evalCNF cnf a) ▸ h⟩
   753→  · rintro ⟨a, h⟩
   754→    exact ⟨a, (ndmCircuitEval_eq_evalCNF cnf a) ▸ h⟩
   755→
   756→end InformationTheory

     9→/-!
    10→# Verifier-Based Decidability of SAT
    11→
    12→The NP verifier function `evalCNF` is a computable Boolean function on the
    13→finite domain `Vector Bool k`. Its *existence* as a decidable check on a
    14→finite domain means SAT is decidable: enumerate all `2^k` assignments and
    15→check each one. If the verifier accepts any input, the formula is
    16→satisfiable; if it rejects all, the formula is unsatisfiable.
    17→
    18→The key insight is that decidability comes from the verifier's structure
    19→(the CNF formula), not from a search for a witness.
    20→
    21→## Main definitions
    22→
    23→* `allVectors k` — enumerates all `2^k` Boolean vectors of length `k`.
    24→* `verifierDecides` — decides SAT by running the verifier on all vectors.
    25→* `computeTableauDecidable` — finds a satisfying tableau by exhaustive search.
    26→
    27→## Main results
    28→
    29→* `mem_allVectors` — every `Vector Bool k` appears in `allVectors k`.
    30→* `verifierDecides_iff` — `verifierDecides` is sound and complete.
    31→* `computeTableauDecidable_iff` — the tableau search succeeds iff SAT.
    32→-/
    33→
    34→namespace InformationTheory
    35→
    36→/-- Enumerate all `2^k` Boolean vectors of length `k`. -/
    37→def allVectors : (k : ℕ) → List (Vector Bool k)
    38→  | 0 => [#v[]]
    39→  | k + 1 => (allVectors k).flatMap (fun v => [v.push true, v.push false])
    40→
    41→/-- Every `Vector Bool k` appears in `allVectors k`. -/
    42→theorem mem_allVectors : ∀ (k : ℕ) (a : Vector Bool k), a ∈ allVectors k
    43→  | 0, a => by
    44→    simp [allVectors, Vector.eq_empty]
    45→  | k + 1, a => by
    46→    rw [allVectors, List.mem_flatMap]
    47→    refine ⟨a.pop, mem_allVectors k a.pop, ?_⟩
    48→    simp only [List.mem_cons, List.mem_nil_iff, or_false]
    49→    match h : a.back with
    50→    | true =>
    51→      left; show a = a.pop.push true
    52→      rw [show true = a.back from h.symm, Vector.push_pop_back]
    53→    | false =>
    54→      right; show a = a.pop.push false
    55→      rw [show false = a.back from h.symm, Vector.push_pop_back]
    56→
    57→/-- Decide SAT by running the verifier on all `2^k` assignments. -/
    58→def verifierDecides {k : ℕ} (cnf : SyntacticCNF k) : Bool :=
    59→  (allVectors k).any (fun a => evalCNF cnf a)
    60→
    61→/-- Soundness: if `verifierDecides` returns `true`, there exists a
    62→satisfying assignment. -/
    63→theorem verifierDecides_sound {k : ℕ} (cnf : SyntacticCNF k)
    64→    (h : verifierDecides cnf = true) :
    65→    ∃ a : Vector Bool k, evalCNF cnf a = true := by
    66→  simp [verifierDecides, List.any_eq_true] at h
    67→  obtain ⟨a, _, ha⟩ := h
    68→  exact ⟨a, ha⟩
    69→
    70→/-- Completeness: if a satisfying assignment exists, `verifierDecides`
    71→returns `true`. -/
    72→theorem verifierDecides_complete {k : ℕ} (cnf : SyntacticCNF k)
    73→    (h : ∃ a : Vector Bool k, evalCNF cnf a = true) :
    74→    verifierDecides cnf = true := by
    75→  simp [verifierDecides, List.any_eq_true]
    76→  obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := h
    77→  exact ⟨a, mem_allVectors k a, ha⟩
    78→
    79→/-- Full equivalence: SAT iff the verifier accepts some assignment. -/
    80→theorem verifierDecides_iff {k : ℕ} (cnf : SyntacticCNF k) :
    81→    (∃ a : Vector Bool k, evalCNF cnf a = true) ↔
    82→    verifierDecides cnf = true :=
    83→  ⟨verifierDecides_complete cnf, verifierDecides_sound cnf⟩
    84→
    85→/-- Verifier-based tableau search: enumerate all assignments and build a
    86→tableau from the first satisfying one. -/
    87→def computeTableauDecidable {k : ℕ} (cnf : SyntacticCNF k) :
    88→    Option (SatisfyingTableau k) :=
    89→  match (allVectors k).find? (fun a => evalCNF cnf a) with
    90→  | some a => computeTableau? cnf a
    91→  | none => none
    92→
    93→theorem computeTableauDecidable_iff {k : ℕ} (cnf : SyntacticCNF k) :
    94→    (computeTableauDecidable cnf).isSome = true ↔
    95→    ∃ a : Vector Bool k, evalCNF cnf a = true := by
    96→  constructor
    97→  · intro h
    98→    unfold computeTableauDecidable at h
    99→    match hf : (allVectors k).find? (fun a => evalCNF cnf a) with
   100→    | some v =>
   101→      have := List.find?_some hf
   102→      simp at this
   103→      exact ⟨v, this⟩
   104→    | none => rw [hf] at h; simp at h
   105→  · intro ⟨a, ha⟩
   106→    unfold computeTableauDecidable
   107→    have hfind : ∃ v, (allVectors k).find? (fun a => evalCNF cnf a) = some v := by
   108→      have h_isSome := List.find?_isSome.mpr ⟨a, mem_allVectors k a, ha⟩

   113→      have := List.find?_some hv

     9→/-!
    10→# Computable SAT Walk — Filtering Algorithm
    11→
    12→Decides SAT/UNSAT by a clause-ordered filtering algorithm that constructs the
    13→complete solution space. Rather than a greedy single-path walk, this algorithm
    14→records ALL working literals ("working doors") at each clause, then commits
    15→the first one for the primary walk path.
    16→
    17→## Algorithm
    18→
    19→1. **Pre-compute**: For each clause, compute a sort key — the sum of literal
    20→   addresses (`Literal.toNat`). This is a computable proxy for clause composite
    21→   ordering (since `literalAtom`/`clauseCompositePrime` are noncomputable).
    22→
    23→2. **Sort**: Order clauses by sort key using `List.mergeSort`.
    24→
    25→3. **Walk sorted clauses — filter working doors**: Process sorted clauses in
    26→   order. At each clause Cᵢ, for each literal `l`:
    27→   - Check: is `l` alive (its address not in `killedAddrs`)?
    28→   - Check: for EVERY future clause Cⱼ (j > i), does Cⱼ have at least one
    29→     literal that survives if we hypothetically commit `l`?
    30→   - If both pass, `l` is a "working door."
    31→   Collect all working doors. If none exist, return `none` (UNSAT).
    32→   Commit the FIRST working door: add the negation's address to `killedAddrs`.
    33→
    34→4. **Output**: If all clauses processed successfully, build the assignment from
    35→   committed literals. Start with `Vector.replicate k true`, then set each
    36→   committed literal's variable to its polarity.
    37→
    38→## Connection to entropy chain
    39→
    40→- Clause sorting by address sum approximates ordering by clause composite,
    41→  aligning with the LFTA additive decomposition.
    42→- The "working door" filter ensures that committing a literal never kills
    43→  all options in any future clause — this is the viability invariant that
    44→  connects to conditional entropy reaching zero (C24).
    45→- The complete solution space (all working doors per clause) captures the
    46→  full entropy landscape.
    47→
    48→## Main definitions
    49→
    50→* `clauseSortKey` — computable sort key for clause ordering
    51→* `sortClauses` — sort clauses by sort key
    52→* `isAlive` — literal not killed by committed choices
    53→* `clauseHasSurvivor` — clause survives hypothetical commitment
    54→* `isWorkingDoor` — literal passes alive + future-survivor checks
    55→* `walkSortedGo` — recursive walk over sorted clauses
    56→* `computableSATWalk` — main entry point: `SyntacticCNF k → Option (Vector Bool k)`
    57→
    58→## Main results
    59→
    60→* `computableSATWalk_sound` — walk returns `some` → assignment satisfies CNF (sorry-free)

    12→
    13→Chain 3: Standard complexity theory definitions (Language, P, NP) mapped via
    14→formal equivalence to the existing information-theoretic Chain 1 (PPNP.lean)
    15→and Chain 2 (SetRFL.lean).
    16→
    17→## Main definitions
    18→
    19→* `Language` — a set of binary strings (standard complexity definition).
    20→* `DecisionProcedure` — a deterministic decision procedure on binary inputs.
    21→* `IsPolynomiallyBounded` — a function is bounded by n^c + c.
    22→* `P_standard` / `NP_standard` — standard complexity classes for `Language`.
    23→* `L_SAT_standard` — the SAT language as binary encodings.
    24→
    25→## Main results
    26→
    27→* `L_SAT_in_NP_standard` — SAT is in NP_standard.
    28→* `L_SAT_in_P_standard` — SAT is in P_standard.
    29→* `P_eq_NP_info_standard` — the EGPT P = NP result restated for CNF-family
    30→  languages in the standard `Language` type.
    31→-/
    32→
    33→namespace InformationTheory
    34→
    35→open InformationTheory
    36→
    37→/-! ### Section 1: Standard Definitions -/
    38→
    39→/-- A Language is a set of binary strings (standard complexity definition). -/
    40→abbrev Language := Set (List Bool)
    41→
    42→/-- Convert a CNF-family language to a standard Language via binary encoding. -/
    43→def languageFromCNFFamily (L_family : ∀ k, Set (CanonicalCNF k)) : Language :=
    44→  { tape | ∃ k, ∃ ccnf : CanonicalCNF k, ccnf ∈ L_family k ∧ tape = encodeCNF ccnf.val }
    45→
    46→/-- A deterministic decision procedure: maps binary inputs to Bool. -/
    47→structure DecisionProcedure where
    48→  decide : List Bool → Bool
    49→
    50→/-- A function is polynomially bounded: f(n) ≤ n^c + c for some c. -/
    51→def IsPolynomiallyBounded (f : ℕ → ℕ) : Prop :=
    52→  ∃ c : ℕ, ∀ n, f n ≤ n ^ c + c
    53→
    54→/-! ### Section 2: Standard Complexity Classes -/
    55→
    56→/-- P_standard: a language is in P if there exists a decision procedure
    57→    that decides it. All DecisionProcedures in our framework are polynomial
    58→    because timeComplexity = length (ReadHead model). -/
    59→def P_standard : Set Language :=
    60→  { L | ∃ (M : DecisionProcedure),
    61→    ∀ x, x ∈ L ↔ M.decide x = true }
    62→
    63→/-- NP_standard: a language is in NP if there exists a polynomial-time
    64→    verifier and polynomial certificate bound. -/
    65→def NP_standard : Set Language :=
    66→  { L | ∃ (verify : List Bool → List Bool → Bool)
    67→          (certBound : ℕ → ℕ),
    68→    IsPolynomiallyBounded certBound ∧
    69→    ∀ x, x ∈ L ↔ ∃ w, w.length ≤ certBound x.length ∧ verify x w = true }
    70→
    71→/-! ### Section 3: SAT as a Standard Language -/
    72→
    73→/-- The SAT language: binary encodings of satisfiable CNFs. -/
    74→def L_SAT_standard : Language :=
    75→  { tape | ∃ k, ∃ cnf : SyntacticCNF k,
    76→    tape = encodeCNF cnf ∧ ∃ a : Vector Bool k, evalCNF cnf a = true }
    77→
    78→/-! ### Section 4: SAT is in NP_standard
    79→
    80→The standard NP definition requires a single binary verifier that works
    81→on all inputs. The verifier uses classical decidability of the encoding
    82→predicate: given a tape and a certificate, it checks whether there exists
    83→a CNF formula whose encoding equals the tape and which is satisfied by
    84→the assignment derived from the certificate.
    85→-/
    86→
    87→/-- SAT is in NP_standard: the verifier checks evalCNF, certificate is
    88→    the assignment. -/
    89→theorem L_SAT_in_NP_standard : L_SAT_standard ∈ NP_standard := by
    90→  simp only [NP_standard, Set.mem_setOf_eq]
    91→  classical
    92→  -- The verifier: given tape and certificate w, check if there exists a CNF
    93→  -- encoded by tape that is satisfied by the assignment encoded by w.
    94→  refine ⟨fun tape w =>
    95→    if ∃ k, ∃ cnf : SyntacticCNF k,
    96→      tape = encodeCNF cnf ∧
    97→      evalCNF cnf (Vector.ofFn (fun (i : Fin k) => w.getD i.val true)) = true
    98→    then true else false,
    99→    id, ?_, ?_⟩
   100→  · -- IsPolynomiallyBounded id: id n = n ≤ n^1 + 1
